question.problem:
The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{-1}{3{x}^{3}+5}$ is

$y=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{3}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{-1}{3{x}^{3}+5} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{-1}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{3{x}^{3}}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{-1}{{x}^{3}})}{(3+\frac{5}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & =\frac{0}{3+0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=0.$
